title: Molecular diagnostics of brain tumors using third-generation sequencing
summary:
The root cause of all brain cancers are modifications to the genetic blueprint (DNA) of a specific brain cell. These alterations lead to uncontrolled growth and, eventually, to the formation of a tumour mass. For most of the last century, these changes could not be observed directly and the diagnosis of a specific type of brain tumour has
been based on observation of tumour tissue through the microscope.
The recent advances in the science of tumour genetics we have yielded much better understanding how such alterations in the DNA can cause the diverse types of brain cancer. This has taught us that the microscopic diagnostic approach alone is not always sufficient. We are combining microscopic inspection with molecular information, and this enables us to offer the right treatment to the right patient at the right time. This approach is also called precision diagnostics.
One powerful approach that is currently changing clinical practice is the classification of tumours by characteristic, so-called epigenetic modifications to the tumor cells DNA. Using machine learning, we can classify thousands of these modifications to achieve a molecular diagnosis. Currently, testing for these epigenetic changes relies on expensive infrastructure in highly specialised laboratories, is time-consuming, and can result in delays that are stressful for patients and detrimental to clinical decision making. Most importantly, in some countries not all patients have equal access to such cutting-edge diagnostics.
This is what we want to change. Our project will make use of a novel and affordable technology that can be adopted by most laboratories and will give all patients rapid access to state-of-the-art diagnostics at reduced cost.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of spinal cord, cranial nerves and other parts of central nervous system

interventions.name: Tumor tissue will be subjected to methylation-based classification by nanopore sequencing.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Female or male individuals with planned biopsy or resection of a suspected brain tumor as part of routine clinical procedures, who have given written informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
None.
